sheets.rejected_alternative: A path-scoped rule under .claude/rules/. It loses because rules trigger on Claude reading a file that matches a glob, not on billing coming up in conversation, and the full explainer would then be injected wholesale every time someone opened a billing file.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The model. Claude decides whether the conversation matches the skill description and loads it or does not; nothing in the harness forces the reference material into a billing discussion.
sheets.context_boundary: Only the skill name and description are resident in the main window at session start. The SKILL.md body loads into the same window when Claude invokes it, and the supporting files cross the boundary only when Claude actually reads them, which is what keeps a long explainer affordable.
sheets.lifecycle: Triggers when Claude matches your prompt against the skill description, then stays in the conversation for the rest of the session. With user-invocable: false it never appears in the user-invocable command list, so it has no user-triggered path at all.
sheets.failure_mode: Advisory, fails open, and quietly. If the description is vague or overlaps another skill, Claude loads the wrong one or none, and because user-invocable: false removes the /name escape hatch you cannot force the load; the recovery is to name the billing topic explicitly or adjust the description. Being model-selected, coverage is never guaranteed for an oblique billing question.
sheets.version_caveat: The controlling frontmatter is user-invocable: false, which keeps the skill loaded and available to Claude while leaving it out of the user-invocable skill list. No minimum version is stated for it in the pages I was able to read; the skills reference page itself could not be retrieved.

scenarios.scenario: The security organization wants identical data-handling reminders and coding-style guidance present in every session on every developer machine, across every repository, and individual developers must not be able to opt out of it loading.

key.primary: Managed policy CLAUDE.md at the OS managed location (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md, Linux /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md), or the claudeMd key in managed-settings.json, deployed via MDM or config management
key.rejected_alternative: Pushing a ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md to every machine via dotfiles
key.rejection_reason: User-scope files belong to the user, who can edit or delete them, and ordinary CLAUDE.md files can be skipped with claudeMdExcludes. The managed policy file loads before user and project scopes in every session on the machine and is the one memory file the docs say cannot be excluded by individual settings.
key.lifecycle: Loaded at the start of every session on the machine, in every repository, before user and project instructions
key.failure_mode: It is still behavioral guidance, not technical enforcement: the docs' own split says anything that must be hard-blocked (tools, commands, paths) belongs in managed settings permissions.deny, not in the managed CLAUDE.md

sheets.primary: A managed-policy CLAUDE.md deployed by IT to /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md on macOS, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md on Linux and WSL, or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md on Windows, or the equivalent claudeMd key inside managed-settings.json, pushed with MDM or Group Policy.
sheets.rejected_alternative: User-scope ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. It is per-developer and developer-writable, so any engineer can edit or delete it, which is exactly the opt-out the security organization needs closed.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, and worth stating plainly: the harness guarantees loading, since a managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by individual settings and claudeMd is honored only in managed and policy settings, but the model owns whether the reminders are actually followed, because CLAUDE.md is not a hard enforcement layer.
sheets.context_boundary: Every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository, in the main conversation window. It loads before user and project CLAUDE.md, so more specific project instructions appear after it in context.
sheets.lifecycle: Loads at the start of every session on every machine where it is deployed, and stops applying only when IT edits or removes the file or the managed setting through the configuration-management channel.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails closed on presence but open on behavior: claudeMdExcludes cannot skip a managed CLAUDE.md, so the text is always there, yet it is behavioral guidance the model can still miss under pressure or conflict. Anything that must actually be blocked (a tool, a command, a file path) belongs in managed settings permissions.deny, which the client enforces regardless of what Claude decides.
sheets.version_caveat: No version gate is stated. The constraints are scope and deployment: claudeMd set in user, project, or local settings has no effect at all, and writing either the managed CLAUDE.md or managed-settings.json requires access to a protected system location, so it needs MDM, Group Policy, Ansible, or similar.

sheets.primary: A managed policy CLAUDE.md deployed by MDM, Group Policy or Ansible to /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md on macOS, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md on Linux and WSL, or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md on Windows. The equivalent is the claudeMd key inside managed-settings.json if you prefer one artifact.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Shipping the same text as ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md through a dotfiles repo, rejected because it lives in a path the developer owns and can edit, delete or exclude, so it is opt-out-able by construction.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, and the split is the whole point. The harness owns loading: a managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be skipped by claudeMdExcludes at any settings layer, so it is guaranteed present. The model owns compliance: what it says is guidance, not a rule the client enforces.
sheets.context_boundary: The main session context window, loaded first in memory order, before user and project CLAUDE.md. Because later files are read last, a project CLAUDE.md that contradicts it appears after it in context.
sheets.lifecycle: Loads at the start of every session on the machine, in every repository, and is re-injected after compaction like other root-level memory. It stops applying only when IT changes or removes the file.
sheets.failure_mode: Guaranteed to load, advisory in effect. If a data-handling reminder must actually prevent something (reading .env files, sending data to an external endpoint), it will not: put that in managed permissions.deny or a PreToolUse hook, and keep the managed CLAUDE.md for behavioral guidance only. It also spends context in every session on every machine, so an overlong policy file quietly degrades adherence everywhere.
sheets.version_caveat: The claudeMd key is honored only in managed and policy settings and is ignored if set in user, project or local settings. On Windows the legacy C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\ location is no longer supported as of v2.1.75, and writing to any of these paths needs administrator or root privileges. Cowork and cloud sessions run on other machines and will not pick up a locally deployed managed file.

sheets.primary: A managed policy CLAUDE.md pushed to every machine by MDM, Group Policy or Ansible, at C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md on Windows, /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md on macOS, /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md on Linux and WSL, or the same content placed in the claudeMd key of managed-settings.json.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A user-scope ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md distributed by a setup script. It loses on the no-opt-out requirement, because that file sits in the developer's own configuration and can be edited, emptied, or deleted with no trace.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, and worth stating precisely. The harness owns loading: a managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded by claudeMdExcludes, and claudeMd is honored only in managed and policy settings, so setting it at user, project or local scope does nothing. The model owns compliance, because CLAUDE.md is behavioral guidance and not a hard enforcement layer.
sheets.context_boundary: The main context window of every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository, loaded at session start ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md so more specific project instructions are read afterward.
sheets.lifecycle: Loads at the start of every session on that machine and applies for the whole session. It stops applying only when whoever administers the machine removes or changes the file at the managed location; individual settings cannot switch it off.
sheets.failure_mode: Loading is guaranteed, effect is advisory, so it fails open on behavior. Data-handling reminders and style guidance can still be ignored, and adherence dilutes as the managed file grows, since longer files reduce compliance. Anything that must actually be prevented belongs in managed settings permissions.deny or a hook rather than in this file.
sheets.version_caveat: No version number is documented for managed policy memory. The gates are deployment and scope: the file must sit at the managed policy path for the OS, or claudeMd must be set in managed or policy settings, and placing claudeMd in user, project, or local settings has no effect. Distribution requires machine-level management such as MDM or Group Policy.

sheets.primary: Enterprise-managed policy memory plus managed settings, deployed by IT or MDM to the system-level managed path (on Windows this is under ProgramData\ClaudeCode, with equivalent system paths on macOS and Linux). Managed policy sits at the top of the precedence chain and is not overridable by user or project files.
sheets.rejected_alternative: A user-level ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md rolled out by script. It reaches every repo on the machine but sits in a user-writable location, so any developer can edit or delete it, which fails the no-opt-out requirement.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Split, and the split is the honest answer. The harness owns that the file loads (precedence plus filesystem ACLs make that non-optional). The model still owns compliance, because the payload is guidance text, and text about data handling is advisory no matter where it is deployed.
sheets.context_boundary: Main session context on every machine, injected at session start ahead of user and project memory. Because it is resident in every window of every session organisation-wide, its token cost is multiplied across the whole company, so brevity here has real economic weight.
sheets.lifecycle: Applies at every session start on any machine where IT has placed the managed file, and stops only when IT removes or updates it. Developers cannot turn it off from within the CLI.
sheets.failure_mode: Fails open on the behaviour it is supposed to guarantee: a model can read a data-handling reminder and still paste a secret into a log. It also fails open if the OS permissions are wrong, since a local administrator can delete the file. Any data-handling rule that must actually hold needs a matching deny rule or PreToolUse hook in the managed settings, not just prose.
sheets.version_caveat: I am reasonably confident that a system-level managed settings file with highest precedence exists, and fairly confident there is a corresponding enterprise policy memory location, but I do not know the exact filenames and paths per platform in the current version, and I do not know whether this is gated to Team or Enterprise plans. Both should be confirmed with the deployment documentation before an org-wide rollout.
